riddles.q: I have rivers without water, forests without trees, and mountains without stone. What am I?
The more you take of me, the more you leave behind in the mud. What am I?
Feed me dry wood and I live; give me clean water and I die. What am I?
I have a needle but I never sew, and I always know which way to go. What am I?
I go up but never come down, no matter how many days the Games last. What am I?
The more of me there is, the less you see. Tributes love to hide in me. What am I?
I'm light as a feather, but even the strongest tribute can't hold me for more than a few minutes. What am I?
I have hands but cannot clap, and I tell you how long until the next cannon. What am I?
I can be cracked, made, told and played. What am I?
What has one eye but cannot see, and helps you fix a torn tent?
I'm full of holes but I still hold water. What am I?
What can run but never walks, has a mouth but never talks, and has a bed but never sleeps?
I follow you all day in the arena but vanish at night. What am I?
What gets wetter the more it dries?
I am always in front of you in the arena but can never be seen. What am I?
What has a neck but no head, and keeps your water safe?
What breaks the moment you say its name? Tributes hiding in bushes need lots of it.
I have keys but open no locks, and the Capitol plays the anthem on me. What am I?
What has many teeth but can't bite, and keeps a tribute's hair camera-ready?
What can you catch but never throw?
What has roots nobody sees, is taller than trees, yet never grows?
What comes down but never goes up, and fills every tribute's canteen?
